title: A bill to amend the White Mountain Apache Tribe Water Rights Quantification Act of 2010 to clarify the use of amounts in the WMAT Settlement Fund.
official_summary:
(Sec. 1) This bill amends the White Mountain Apache Tribe Water Rights Quantification Act of 2010 to specify that settlement funds may be used for the planning, design, and construction of the tribe's rural water system.

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Act of August 9, 1955 (commonly known as the Long-Term Leasing Act) to expand the land of the Pueblo of Santa Clara and Ohkay Owingeh pueblo that may be leased for up to 99 years with the approval of the Department of the Interior, from lands held in trust, to all of the lands of the Pueblo of Santa Clara and Ohkay Owingeh pueblo.

summary.headline: This law lets the White Mountain Apache Tribe use its water settlement money for its rural water system and lets two New Mexico pueblos lease more of their land for long terms.
summary.what_it_does: Section 1 changes the 2010 White Mountain Apache Tribe Water Rights Quantification Act so that settlement funds can be spent on planning, designing, and building the tribe's rural water system. Section 2 changes the Long-Term Leasing Act so that the Pueblo of Santa Clara and Ohkay Owingeh can lease all of their lands, not just trust lands, for up to 99 years with Interior Department approval.

who_it_affects.how: The tribe can use its WMAT Settlement Fund money to plan, design, and build its rural water system.

who_it_affects.group: Pueblo of Santa Clara and Ohkay Owingeh members
who_it_affects.how: The two pueblos can lease all of their lands for up to 99 years, with Interior Department approval, instead of only their trust lands.

who_it_affects.group: Lessees and developers who may lease pueblo land
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to enter long-term leases on a wider set of pueblo lands, subject to Interior Department approval.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect on August 1, 2018, the date it was enacted.
